reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) discusses general MCE phenomena and composition-dependent transitions in other systems but provides no specific support for the role of microstructural heterogeneities in FeMnNiGeSi alloys, the effect of rapid solidification on pinning, or the predicted outcomes of surface treatment. The key premises rely on uncited mechanistic assumptions.
premises: Microstructural heterogeneities (grain boundaries, strain, defects) pin the magnetostructural transition, causing sharp first-order change and hysteresis
Rapid solidification (arc-melting/melt-spinning) produces these heterogeneities in the as-deposited state
Modifying near-surface microstructure (e.g., by annealing) can reduce pinning and induce a more diffuse transition
A more diffuse transition lowers hysteresis and broadens the entropy change peak
Surface treatment increases surface-to-volume ratio, improving heat-exchange rate
